A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OPSD research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, references, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original Qwen3 training and evaluation results, including mathematical benchmark scores, token-efficiency comparisons, and generation-length and objective ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark and ablation results and reports revised scores and learning curves in Table 2 and Figure 3.

M1.justification: The student rollouts, privileged teacher conditioning, full-vocabulary divergence loss, and sampled-token alternative remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 is condensed without changing its procedure. Teacher prefilling and the prompt-format mismatch are clarified implementation details, not demonstrated method changes.

E1.justification: Both versions train on the mathematical subset of OpenThoughts and evaluate on AIME 2024, AIME 2025, HMMT 2025, and AMO-Bench. No additional dataset, domain, or task scenario is evaluated.

E2.justification: v2 adds SFT to Figure 3's accuracy-versus-training-steps comparison, which previously displayed only OPSD and GRPO. Comparator membership in Table 2, Table 3, and Figure 4 is retained. STaR and the newly discussed self-distillation methods are not added as empirical baselines.

E3.justification: The headline efficiency comparison changes OPSD's rollout cap from 2048 to 1024 tokens; Appendix B specifies a 2e-4 learning rate for this run versus v1's tabulated 2e-5. Table 2's evaluation temperature changes from 1.2 to 1.0, and OPSD's training sampling temperature changes from 1.2 to 1.1. These materially revise reported comparison conditions, without establishing which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix B adds a qualitative learning-rate sensitivity finding: 2e-4 works better than 2e-5 with 1024-token generations. No supporting sensitivity table is supplied. The generation-length ablation in Figure 4 and full-vocabulary versus sampled-token ablation in Table 3 retain their results.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training-seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. v2's statement that OPSD does not significantly outperform GRPO is not accompanied by a new statistical procedure. Evaluation still uses 16 samples per prompt.

E6.justification: Figure 3 replaces the OPSD and GRPO learning curves, adds SFT results, and revises reported token efficiency from 4–8x to 8–12x under changed settings. Table 2 revises OPSD's 4B average from 50.6 to 50.4 and 1.7B average from 30.4 to 30.0; its 1.7B HMMT25 score changes from 25.8 to 25.0, below the retained base score of 25.4. These revise central empirical evidence, rather than establish same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: New Appendix C adds STaR's indicator-reward objective and its policy-gradient derivation in Equations 10–11, together with an explicit expected-reward formulation for OPSD. This is a limited formal extension of the existing policy-gradient discussion; the original OPSD objectives remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The introduction narrows the accuracy claim from outperforming GRPO to matching it. Conversely, the abstract strengthens the token-efficiency claim from 4–8x to 8–12x. The central contribution of privileged-context self-distillation and the conclusion's broader claims are retained.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly discusses the 1.7B model's HMMT25 underperformance and hypothesizes noisy supervision when capacity is insufficient. It also treats prompt formats as optimizable design choices and expands the dense-feedback interpretation through comparison with STaR. The original limitations are retained in Appendix A, not removed.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link and discloses the template-free student versus thinking-template teacher mismatch. It newly documents per-task best-checkpoint selection every 100 steps through 1500 steps and clarifies that the teacher does not generate tokens. These substantially improve reproducibility information. The appendix also adds H100 hardware, while v1's warmup and cosine-schedule statement is removed.

R1.justification: Section 5 substantially sharpens positioning against context distillation, STaR/ReST, and in-context editing through distinctions between on-policy/off-policy and soft/hard supervision. It adds soft bootstrapping and concurrent SDPO/SDFT discussions, alongside other citations. Appendix C further develops the relationship to STaR, making this a substantive positioning revision.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized method and experiment clarifications, condenses Algorithm 1, and rewrites and reorders related-work paragraphs. Limitations move from Section 7 to Appendix A, an Impact Statement is added, and the appendix gains named sections. Most of the original narrative remains intact.

P2.justification: Figure 3 is redrawn with an SFT curve, an explicit OPSD generation-length legend, and revised axes and caption. Figure 4 is resized and relocated; Table 2's caption expands; appendix configuration tables are reordered and rearranged. The overall visual design and remaining displays are largely retained.

improvement.justification: v2 improves transparency by disclosing the actual prompt mismatch and best-checkpoint selection protocol, and it calibrates the GRPO comparison more cautiously. Clearer distinctions from related self-distillation work also improve interpretation. These benefits outweigh the limited loss of scheduler detail. The stronger efficiency multiplier uses changed settings, and uncertainty remains unquantified, so the revision supports a limited quality improvement rather than a demonstrated broad performance advance.
